Guidance for external:

- Share deltas relative to our current production baseline kernel path (not absolute ms unless they’re under NDA).
- Call out that TTFT can be flat-to-slightly worse in some short prompts due to launch overhead / scheduling mix.

Jonas: can you provide the safe perf bands we’re using in the exec readout (H100) + any “do not claim” items?



From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, Feb 22, 2026 at 9:26 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: FP8 vs INT8 perf numbers on H100 + rollout timing

Here are externally-shareable bands (H100 only) with required caveats.

OK to share (as ranges):
- FP8: +15–30% decode throughput (tokens/sec), typically -2% to +6% TTFT (depending on prompt length + concurrency)
- INT8: +8–18% decode throughput, TTFT typically -3% to +4%

Required caveats:
- These are from Redwood’s benchmark suite v3 (representative of our hosted traffic mix); customer workloads can shift wins.
- Largest wins show up in decode-heavy regimes and moderate+ concurrency; smaller wins for very short prompts.
- For INT8 specifically: we require calibration + quick quality sanity eval for model/workload before default enablement.

Do NOT claim:
- “INT8 always faster than FP8” (not true)
- “No quality impact” (we’ve seen model-specific regressions, esp long-context / structured outputs)

If you want, I can send a one-pager excerpt PDF you can attach.

I’d describe timing as “weeks, not months” for H100, but still staged + reversible.

Subject: Re: Request: FP8 vs INT8 perf numbers on H100 + rollout timing

Hi Samir — sharing what we can externally today (ranges + methodology caveats). I’ve attached a short excerpt with the same content.

H100 perf deltas (vs our current production baseline kernel path; benchmark suite v3; mixed prefill/decode workloads):
- FP8: +15–30% decode throughput (tokens/sec). TTFT typically -2% to +6% depending on prompt length + concurrency.
- INT8: +8–18% decode throughput. TTFT typically -3% to +4%.

Caveats (important):
- Wins are largest in decode-heavy regimes and moderate+ concurrency; very short prompts can show smaller gains and sometimes slightly worse TTFT due to launch/scheduling overhead.
- INT8 requires calibration, and we recommend a quick quality sanity run on your prompt set before enabling broadly (we’ve seen model/workload-specific quality regressions in long-context / structured-output style tasks).

Rollout timing:
- Hosted (H100): in perf-canary now; staged region/model expansion next week if thresholds hold; moving toward phased “on by default” by model after eval sign-off.
- Dedicated (H100): we can enable FP8/INT8 per-deployment behind flags sooner as an opt-in, with baseline capture + rollback criteria. For INT8, we’d include calibration + sanity eval as part of the enablement.

If helpful, we can run a small pilot benchmark on your representative traffic shape (prompt length distribution + concurrency targets) and share absolute numbers under NDA.

Best,
Avery

—
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>

Yes on both.

1) Hosted expansion is gated on canary thresholds (TTFT/TPOT + error rate) with automatic rollback if we breach. The “next week” step is contingent on canary staying within bounds across regions/models.

2) Dedicated: starting with FP8-only is the normal path. We’ll lock in a baseline first, enable FP8 behind flags, monitor, and then optionally test INT8 later once calibration + a quick quality sanity run on your prompts are complete.

If you can share (even rough) targets for:
- p95 TTFT
- steady-state tokens/sec / concurrency
- typical prompt + generation lengths
…I can pull in our runtime team for a 30-min working session and we can scope the pilot.

Best,
Avery
